title: cap-overview shows amounts in `cents`
caps:usage hands cap callbacks a tenant-scoped db without unsafeRaw
detail: On the own-tenant call and on the SystemAdmin override, `usage(db, tenantId)` and `limit(tier, { db })` now receive a tenant-mode `TenantDb` that returns only the target tenant's rows plus reference rows of `SYSTEM_TENANT_ID`. Before, both got the unfiltered system-mode db, and an app callback without a `tenantId` filter leaked counts of every tenant. The handler no longer declares an `escapeHatch`, so `db.unsafeRaw()` inside these callbacks throws an `AccessDeniedError`; COUNT, SUM and AVG go through `db.count` and `db.aggregate`. `tenant-caps:list` is unchanged and still hands the system-mode db to `usage`, `usageBatch`, `limit` and `limitBatch`.
migration: A `CapSpec.usage()` or `limit()` that calls `db.unsafeRaw()` switches to `db.count` or `db.aggregate`. Keep the explicit `tenantId` filter, because tenant-caps:list still needs it. No callback in kumiko-studio or offlot-app uses `unsafeRaw()` or reads across tenants.

title: Tenant caps list sorts by key and searches through the search index
detail: Tenant names are ciphertext at rest, so the list used to decrypt every tenant on each call (the default sort was the name, and every search filtered decrypted names). The default sort is now the tenant `key`, each row carries `key`, and `sort: "name"` is rejected with a 400 like any other unsupported sort field. A search goes through the app's SearchAdapter, where the tenant name is already indexed for `tenant:query:list`, and answers 422 `search_adapter_not_wired` when no adapter is wired; more than 1000 candidate hits set `searchTruncated`. Only the names of the returned page are decrypted.
migration: Callers that send `sort: "name"` to `cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list` drop it or send `sort: "key"`. Apps that search this list wire a SearchAdapter. No caller in kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-platform, kumiko-studio or the app repos sends `sort: "name"`.

Tenant caps list decrypts only the visible page
tenant-caps:list pages by offset and rejects cursor
detail: The cap overview list showed page 1 on every page because the pager sends offset and the query only read cursor. tenant-caps:list now takes offset like the pager; a cursor in the payload is rejected with a 400 validation error and sort is an enum of the sortable fields. The unused cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor and sortFieldUnsupported keys are gone.
migration: Callers of cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list must send offset instead of cursor, and only a sortable field name as sort. Apps that override the removed i18n keys cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor or cap-overview.errors.sortFieldUnsupported can delete them. No caller in the kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-platform, kumiko-studio or app repos sends a cursor or defines these keys.

title: Cap overview lists no destroyed tenants
caps:usage and my-caps default to admin roles; widen with usageVisibleTo
detail: `createCapOverviewFeature` gets `usageVisibleTo?: readonly string[]`. Without it, the `caps:usage` query and the `my-caps` screen accept `access.admin` (TenantAdmin, Admin, SystemAdmin) instead of every tenant member. The screen and the query share the resolved roles. Only built-in roles are accepted (User, Member, Editor, Admin, TenantAdmin, SystemAdmin); an unknown or empty list throws at feature definition. The SystemAdmin `tenantId` override and the platform-wide screens are unchanged. The `MY_CAPS_ACCESS_ROLES` export is replaced by `DEFAULT_CAP_USAGE_ROLES` (the admin default), and `myCapsScreen` by `createMyCapsScreen(roles)`.
migration: Apps whose regular members should keep seeing their usage pass `createCapOverviewFeature({ ..., usageVisibleTo: ["User", "Editor", "Admin", "TenantAdmin", "SystemAdmin"] })`. Code that imported `MY_CAPS_ACCESS_ROLES` (handlers or nav entries mirroring the screen rule) imports `DEFAULT_CAP_USAGE_ROLES` for the admin default, or reuses the same `usageVisibleTo` array it passed to the feature.
